glosses: a diminutive, Katyusha, of the female given names Ка́тя (Kátja), Екатери́на (Jekaterína), or Катери́на (Katerína)
a Russian folk song composed in 1938.
a type of artillery rocket launcher consisting of an array of rockets mounted on a truck, originated in the Soviet Union, named after the song.

уменьш.-ласк. Катя
неисч., популярная советская патриотическая песня М. Блантера на слова М. Исаковского
A transliteration of the Russian or Ukrainian female given name Катюша (Katjuša)
A type of artillery rocket launcher consisting of an array of rockets mounted on a truck, originated in the Soviet Union.

examples.text: The Russian Katyusha is a multiple rocket thrower of which nothing is known except what can be seen on released photographs.

glosses: A type of rocket which can be launched from a Katyusha.

examples.text: The development of these projectors was spurred During World War II, the Soviet Union fired Katyusha rockets from the ground or truck mounted racks. The standard Katyushas were 6 feet long, weighed 92.5 pounds, and had a range of 3 miles.

A curfew was clamped down on December 21 upon the Arab village of Battir, south of Jerusalem, near where security forces on December 20 found the rocket launchers from which two Katyushas were earlier fired into a Jerusalem residential area.

examples.text: Wegen des charakteristischen pfeifenden Geräusches das die Raketen beim Start verursachten, wurde die Waffe Stalinorgel genannt.
„Unter dem Heulen der Stalinorgel, im mörderischen Granathagel, eingeklemmt zwischen zerfetzten Menschenleibern war für erhebene Gedanken kein Platz.“
„Die Sowjets beschossen die Stadt, die kurz darauf fallen sollte, aus Stalinorgeln.“

воен., разг., устар. солдатский набор для прикуривания

examples.text: Гремела у каждого в кармане ещё одна прославленная «катюша» ― прибор для прикуривания: обугленный трут, здоровый кремень и железное кресало.
Вместо спичек были «катюши» — кремень, да железка, да кусок трута.
